summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for government modernization and regulated-workflow software. The best reference leader is Tyler Technologies because it is a public-sector-only vertical software vendor. The underfollowed lane contains smaller or less broadly followed vendors where policy, public-safety regulation, agency digitization, procurement cycles, FedRAMP/cloud compliance, and state/local budget flows can be material to revenue. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Layer 1B expands the universe around scarce or sticky public-sector workflow software vendors rather than generic AI or defense primes. The two-lane funnel keeps Tyler Technologies as the reference pure-play public-sector software leader, then surfaces underfollowed or smaller names where policy, public safety, digital evidence, cleared-labor constraints, and transportation grants can create administrative or compliance workflow demand. This pass is research-only and does not make trading recommendations. Layer 1B expanded the universe around public-sector modernization software with a two-lane funnel. Tyler Technologies is retained as the pure-play reference anchor, while Appian, Cellebrite, and SoundThinking form the underfollowed discovery lane. The strongest underfollowed fits are vendors whose products sit inside agency workflows that regulation and government-spending complexity can make stickier: procurement, grants, case management, digital investigations, public safety analytics, FedRAMP/cloud authorization, and compliance-heavy agency operations.
